name: Do you need a permit for a home addition in Pasadena or Glendale?

mainEntity.name: Do you need a permit for a home addition in Pasadena or Glendale?
mainEntity.text: Do you need a permit for a home addition in Pasadena or Glendale?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most home additions in Pasadena and Glendale require permits, especially when the project changes the building footprint, roofline, structural walls, electrical service, plumbing, or HVAC. Even a smaller extension may need permits if it affects setbacks, fire-rated assemblies, or exterior openings. Cities in the Los Angeles area can also have different plan-check requirements, so a project that is straightforward in one city may take longer in another. Homeowners should expect drawings, structural details, and possibly energy-compliance documents before construction begins. It helps to verify whether the project is a simple interior remodel or a true addition, because that distinction changes the approval process. A contractor familiar with the local city should be able to tell you what documents are needed and whether design revisions are likely before the permit is issued.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, most home additions in Pasadena and Glendale require permits because they change the structure, footprint, electrical, plumbing, or mechanical systems. Even smaller projects can need plan review if they affect walls, windows, rooflines, setbacks, or fire safety requirements.
